body: On 7 Jan 2009 chairman B. Ramalinga Raju confessed that Rs 5,040 cr of the Rs 5,361 cr cash and bank balance at Sep-2008 did not exist (total manipulation ~Rs 7,000 cr incl. fake interest accrual, understated liabilities, overstated debtors). Stock: 52-week high ~Rs 544 (2008) -> Rs 179 (6 Jan 2009) -> Rs 39.95 close on 7 Jan (-78%) -> ~Rs 6-7 intraday within days; Tech Mahindra bought control in Apr 2009 at Rs 58/share. Visible-in-advance flags: (1) a huge cash pile earning low interest (other income far below what Rs 5,000 cr+ should yield) while the company did not pay large dividends or buy back stock; (2) debtor days above peers; (3) promoter holding fell from ~25% (2001) to ~8.6% (2008) and much of it was pledged; (4) 16 Dec 2008 board approved a $1.6 bn purchase of promoter-family Maytas Properties/Infra (unrelated real estate) -- reversed in 12 hours after investor revolt; (5) World Bank debarred Satyam in Dec 2008; (6) independent directors resigned in late Dec 2008. Auditor PwC signed off for years (later penalised by SEBI/US PCAOB). Who spotted it: institutional investors who revolted against Maytas; some analysts flagged the unexplained cash yield. Lesson: test that cash earns market interest (interest income / average cash), compare promoter holding trend and pledges, and treat any related-party acquisition proposal by a cash-rich company as a disqualifier.

data.early_signals: low yield on reported cash; falling+pledged promoter stake; Maytas related-party deal; World Bank debarment; director resignations
data.end_price: ~Rs 6-7 intraday low Jan 2009; Rs 58 Tech Mahindra deal
data.lesson: Fake cash shows up as low other income; related-party deals by cash-rich firms are a disqualifier

title: Satyam Computer fraud (Jan 2009)
